body.statement: The estimator in def:adjoint-covariance retains the finite-bandwidth harmonic translation score and every generated-target cross product and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). The harmonic variance and its Green cross-covariances vanish after division by \(L_n\), but retaining them makes the finite-bandwidth covariance exact. Uniform positive definiteness of \(V(P)\), covariance consistency, and \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\) imply \(\max_{1\le j\le J}\lVert(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R})^{-1}-V_j(P)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so the ridge is asymptotically negligible while every block inverse exists in every sample.
body.justification: Cross-fitting reduces the empirical covariance step to a conditional variance bound once normalized corrected-score consistency is proved.
body.gap: The adjoint score presently corresponds to an incomplete derivative and moving-pole stability is unproved.
body.consumer: The ridge totalizes computation, but feasible covariance consistency remains open.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove normalized opposite-fold score consistency for the corrected harmonic, coefficient, generated-target, and moving-pole scores.
obligation.obstruction: Cross-fitting turns covariance estimation into a conditional law-of-large-numbers problem, but the necessary normalized pilot-score comparison is one of the unresolved uniform critical estimates and the current adjoint score is based on the incomplete derivative.
obligation.attempted: The conditional covariance identity and the fourth-moment variance rate were derived, reducing consistency to the exact normalized score comparison and the population covariance limit.
obligation.partial_result:
For the cross-fitted multiplier score, conditioning on the training folds makes the evaluation-fold observations independent.  For every matrix entry, the fourth-moment envelope would give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left[
 L_n^{-1}\frac n{n_g}\frac1{n_g}
 \sum_{i=1}^{n_g}
 \widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})
 \widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})^{\mathsf T}
 \ \middle|\ \text{training folds}\right]
 \leq \frac{C}{n h_n^2L_n^2}=o(1).
\tag{13}
\]
Moreover, if
\[
 L_n^{-1/2}\lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz makes the normalized difference between pilot and population second moments \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).  Fold centering is also negligible.  Equations (13) and the score comparison would reduce \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}\) to \(\Sigma_{h_n}(P)\).  The unresolved ingredient is precisely that score comparison for the corrected harmonic and moving-pole terms.
